newsitem.title: UK: European bourses mixed, mark continues to recover.
newsitem.headline: European bourses mixed, mark continues to recover.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Thursday after Wall Street's third loss in a row overnight and the mark continued to recover against the dollar .

After trading lower early on, leading London stocks moved marginally into positive territory helped by a boost to the value of chemicals giant ICI, which gained after its third-quarter profits, while lower, contained no new shocks for the stock market.

Dealers said despite the weak performance in New York -- where the Dow ended 25.34 points lower at 6,036.46 after being down nearly 70 points at one time -- the market was underpinned by steady government bonds and a firm overnight performance from Treasuries.
ICI dominated early dealing, confounding market expectations with a 20-1/2 pence rise to 796 after the group announced third-quarter results at the lower end of forecasts.

"ICI aside, the rest of the market is not looking so bright and I can't see this one stock pulling the entire market up," one trader said, noting that gainers and losers were roughly balanced and trading appeared quiet.

German shares, which were stronger in pre-bourse electronic trade, opened bourse trading half a percent down. But dealers said they saw the market stable or recovering from the tumble taken on Wednesday by software group SAP AG after a profits warning.
Frankfurt traders said they would be keeping a keen eye on the U.S. market and the bourse could post further losses if Wall Street traded weaker again on Thursday.
French shares started lower and turned mixed in line with futures contracts on profit-taking on the last day of the October account. The main CAC-40 moved up somewhat from a negative start.

The mark's gradual recovery against the dollar this week was bolstered by official comments indicating the Bundesbank council, which was meeting on Thursday, would not cut German interest rates again.

The mark was also helped by a surprise cut in the Italian discount rate late on Wednesday. By 1015 GMT the lira had dipped to 1007.00 against the mark compared with 1003.10 in late Europe on Wednesday.

Lingering speculation of a cut in German rates at the regular Thursday Bundesbank meeting was dashed on Wednesday by the central bank's chief economist, Otmar Issing, and its vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum.

Issing said key German rates were at historic lows and nothing more should be expected or was necessary. Gaddum said current interest rate levels were correct and the central bank wanted to keep rates steady for as long as possible.
The dollar was trading at 1.5193 marks compared with 1.5225 late on Wednesday. Chartists predicted there would be strong support for the dollar at 1.5180.
Against the yen, the dollar was at 112.73 compared with 113.05 late Wednesday.

Meanwhile, Sweden's Riksbank (central bank) cut its deposit and lending rates by half a percentage point on Thursday and its key repo rate by a quarter of a percentage point. The Swedish crown eased slightly in reaction to 4.3315 to the mark from 4.3200 earlier.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5193 marks and 112.73 yen compared with 1.5225 and 113.05 yen on Wednesday.
STOCKS AT 1015 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 1.9 points at 4030.3
Germany's DAX index was down 17.7 at 2681.83.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 0.85 at 2,149.71.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $383.70 an ounce in the morning, compared with $383.55 at the close in London on Wednesday. Silver was also firmer at $4.99.
